paragraphs.text: All were involved, because of the same body politic: and every man is bound to be his brother’s keeper, to see that the law be not only observed but preserved: since one sinner may destroy much good. {Ecc 9:18} Propter contagionem peccati. {a}
paragraphs.anchor: But the children of Israel committed.

paragraphs.text: He was well descended, but became a stain to his ancestors by his covetousness, which was the worse in him, because he had, of his own, oxen, asses, sheep, &c. {Jos 6:24 Pro 6:30} The devil knew his temper, felt which way his pulse beat, and accordingly fitted him with an object, set a prize before him: hence he is called "the tempter" {Mat 4:3}
paragraphs.anchor: For Achan, the son of Carmi, &c.

paragraphs.text: Who all smarted for this one man’s sin: as the neck is seared and rowled oft for the rheum that runneth down into the eyes: and as a vein is opened in the arm to turn the course of the blood, or to ease the pain of the head.
paragraphs.anchor: And the anger of the Lord was kindled against the children of Israel.

paragraphs.text: {a} Propter arctam coniuactionem.
Called elsewhere Hai, and Aija; {Gen 12:8 Neh 11:31} by the Septuagint, Gae; by Sulpitius, Geth.
paragraphs.anchor: To Ai.

paragraphs.text: This Bethel, when Jeroboam had defiled it with his idolatry, is in scorn called Bethaven, the house of vanity. {Hos 4:15; Hos 10:5; 2Ki 23:13} Har hamishca, Mount Olivet, is for the like cause called in derision Har hamaschith, the Mount of Corruption.
paragraphs.anchor: Which is beside Bethavon, on the east side of Bethel.

paragraphs.text: But better they had, as it happened, in some respects. God’s holy hand was in it, and his holy will must be done and suffered.
paragraphs.anchor: Let not all the people go up.

paragraphs.text: Their sins having betrayed them into the hands of divine justice, the victory was abandoned, and sent away to the enemy; as that noble General Trajan told Valens, the Arrian emperor, when he had been defeated by the Goths in the very first battle, as these Israelites also were. {a}
paragraphs.anchor: And they fled before the men of Ai.

paragraphs.text: {a} Niceph., lib. xiii. cap. 40.
Not in fight, but in flight; for they stood not out the first shock.
paragraphs.anchor: And the men of Ai smote of them.

paragraphs.text: “ A cane non magno saepe tenetur aper. ”
i.e., A place of breakings or shiverings: this made them "sick at heart," according to Amo 6:6. {See Trapp on "Amo 6:6"}
paragraphs.anchor: Even unto Shebarim

paragraphs.text: They were not more discomfited than discouraged: because they saw that God was displeased, and for the time departed. A little water in a leaden vessel is very heavy: so is a small affliction from an offended Father. "Be not thou a terror to me," saith Jeremiah, {Jer 17:17} and then I care not greatly what befalleth me.
paragraphs.anchor: Wherefore the hearts of the people melted.

paragraphs.text: In token that his heart was rent with grief and anguish.
paragraphs.anchor: And Joshua rent his clothes.

paragraphs.text: “ Sic faciles motus mens generosa capit. ”

Baron Marshal of France and other profane men derided the Earl of Essex’s prayers and tears at his death, as more befitting a silly minister than a stout warrior: {a} as if the fear of God’s wrath were not a Christian man’s fortitude. Joshua was man good enough, and yet, &c.

So long they continued their fast. Let our fasts be, according to that old canon, Usque dum stellae in caelo appareant, till the stars appear in the sky. The Turks hold out their fasts so long, in the hottest and longest days of summer, not tasting so much as a cup of water. {b}
paragraphs.anchor: Until the eventide.

paragraphs.text: {a} Camden’s Elisab.
{b} Turk. Hist.
This expostulation, though of a good intention, is not altogether sinless, but savoureth somewhat of human frailty and weakness of faith; some gravel goeth along with this pure water.
paragraphs.anchor: Alas! O Lord God, wherefore, &c.

paragraphs.text: How shall I stop the open mouths of our reproachers? Thus he filleth his mouth with arguments; rousing up himself and wrestling with God.
paragraphs.anchor: O Lord! what shall I say? &c.

paragraphs.text: This was Joshua’s chief care, - lest God should suffer in the glory of his power and truth. It is the ingenuity of saints, to study God’s share more than their own, and to desire far more that God may be glorified than themselves gratified; they drown all self-respects in his honour, and can believe, when things are at worst, that Christ’s cause shall prevail. There are many golden sayings of Luther sounding to this sense, in his epistles to Melancthon especially, such as a man would fetch upon his knees from Rome or Jerusalem, saith one.
paragraphs.anchor: And what wilt thou do unto thy great name?

paragraphs.text: Get thee up: wherefore liest thou? &c., ] q.d., It is well to pray thus, but it is not all; something else is to be done. Ora et labora, pray and search, pray and fight, up and be doing, for "I will surely be with thee." {Exo 14:14} Our Edward I, A.D. 1299, leading his army forth against the Scots, his horse, as he was putting foot in the stirrup, threw him to the earth, and striking with the hinder heels, brake two of his ribs: who nevertheless upon the same horse proceeded in person to the battle, and overthrew them at Falkirk: {a} so did Joshua, the men of Ai; being rather wakened than weakened by his late loss: and this was the fruit of prayer.
{a} Speed, p. 656.
See Jos 7:1.
paragraphs.anchor: Israel hath sinned.

paragraphs.text: God aggravateth Achan’s sin by the several circumstances, laying open how many transgressions were wrapped up in that sin of his, as Lev 16:21. This Achan himself should have done, and so prevented the Lord; {1Co 11:31} which because he did not, God did it for him: as because the scholar will not parse his lesson, scan his verses, the master will do it for him to his cost.
paragraphs.anchor: For they have even taken of the accursed thing, &c.

paragraphs.text: Sin is that great discord maker, hell-hag, cut-throat, troubler, mother of all mischief: and that was a very good answer of an English captain at the loss of Calais, when a proud Frenchman tauntingly asked, When will ye fetch Calais again? the reply was, Quando peccata vestra erunt nostris graviora, When your sins shall weigh down ours.
paragraphs.anchor: Therefore the children of Israel could not stand.

paragraphs.text: That God which, for ten righteous men, would have spared the five wicked cities, would not be content to drown that one sin of Achan among the righteous.
paragraphs.anchor: Neither will I be with you any more.

paragraphs.text: Come before God with the best preparations you can make. That "God that is holy is to be sanctified in righteousness." {Isa 5:16} And he will be "sanctified of all them that draw nigh unto him" {Lev 10:3}
paragraphs.anchor: Up, sanctify the people, and say, Sanctify, &c.

paragraphs.text: Christ, at last day, will do, saith a divine, as Joshua here did: there were many brought together, and all to find out one. So shall all then appear: out of them a small number deducted that have heard of Christ; out of them, those that have professed him; and out of them, those that have professed in sincerity; a small few.
paragraphs.anchor: The tribe which the Lord taketh shall come according to their families.

paragraphs.text: After that he is first stoned with stones as a presumptuous offender, {Num 15:30; Num 15:35} who is a kind of blasphemer, {Eze 20:37} and his sin such, as is not to be expiated by sacrifice.
paragraphs.anchor: Shall be burnt with fire.

paragraphs.text: His children also, as part of his goods, and infected with the contagion of his sin. Besides, they owed a death to God, who might require that debt when and how he would; neither could there be any iniquity with the Lord, since his holy will is not only recta sed regula, right, but the rule of right: neither is it for silly men to reprehend what they cannot comprehend.
paragraphs.anchor: He and all that he hath.

paragraphs.text: Or, Wickedness, which is folly in the abstract: like as righteousness is right-wiseness, and a righteous man a right-wise-man, as in our old English books we find it printed.
paragraphs.anchor: And because he hath wrought folly.

paragraphs.text: Quorum ingentia beneficia, ingentia flagitia, ingentia igitur supplicia: men’s offences are increased by their obligations.
paragraphs.anchor: In Israel.

paragraphs.text: See chap. vi. 12. Long lying in bed is reckoned among the works of the flesh, and forbidden as such. {Rom 13:13} {See Trapp on "Rom 13:13"}
paragraphs.anchor: So Joshua rose up early.

paragraphs.text: Yet all this while Achan repenteth not, confesseth not his fault. The devil had gagged him, and his heart was hardened by the deceitfulness of that cursed sin of covetousness, the property whereof is first to turn men’s hearts into earth and mud, and afterwards to freeze and congeal them into steel and adamant.
paragraphs.anchor: And Zabdi was taken.

paragraphs.text: Secret sinners are loath to be discovered, but their sin shall find them out, and iniquity, if unrepented of, be their ruin. "He that hideth his sins shall not prosper," {Pro 28:13} because he putteth God to his proofs, as Achan, and as those in Jeremiah did. {Jer 2:35}
paragraphs.anchor: And Achan, the son of Carmi.

paragraphs.text: See for explication of this expression, 1Sa 6:5 Jer 13:16 Joh 9:24. It seemeth to have been a solemn kind of form among that people, whereby a man was urged to confess his sin before the Lord, who knoweth all thy business; wherefore reverence his majesty, and give him the glory of his omniscience; choose rather to tell all openly, than to lie before him, or to keep a senseless silence, as Judas did. {Joh 13:21 Mat 26:24}
paragraphs.anchor: My son, give, I pray thee, glory to the Lord.

paragraphs.text: That thou mayest have mercy. {Pro 28:13 1Jn 1:9} In men’s courts the best plea, saith Quintilian, is Non feci, Not guilty: but here, Ego feci, miserere. This, good Joshua knew, and was therefore thus earnest with Achan to confess his sin, though he knew it, and was resolved he should die for it.
paragraphs.anchor: And make confession unto him.

paragraphs.text: Now at length he confesseth. Nunquam sero si serio. Satan knoweth that there is no way to purge the sin sick soul but upwards. He therefore holdeth the lips close as long as he can, that the heart may not disburden itself.
paragraphs.anchor: Indeed I have sinned.

paragraphs.text: Millions have died of the wound in the eye. Covetousness is called "the lust of the eye," {1Jn 2:16} and by this window much wickedness windeth itself into the heart, said the wise heathen.
paragraphs.anchor: When I saw, &c.

paragraphs.text: It was a matter of haste, that justice might be speedily executed, and God’s favour re-obtained.
paragraphs.anchor: And they ran unto the tent.

paragraphs.text: Sin not therefore in hope of secrecy: or if you have, take up the matter in God’s privy chamber of mercy by true repentance, that so his open judicial proceeding in court may be stopped. See 1Co 11:31.
paragraphs.anchor: And they took them out of the midst of the tent.

paragraphs.text: Sed non nisi coactus, as that emperor said when he signed a writ of execution.
paragraphs.anchor: Took Achan the son of Zerah.

paragraphs.text: “ Ille dolet quoties cogitur esse ferox. ”
{See Trapp on "Jos 7:15"}
paragraphs.anchor: And his sons and daughters.

paragraphs.text: There was a young man among the Suitzers that went about to trouble and alter their free state. Him they condemned to death, and appointed his father for executioner, because he bred him no better. {a}
paragraphs.anchor: Why hast thou troubled us?

paragraphs.text: {a} Bishop Ridley told Stephen Gardiner that it was the hand of God that he was now in prison, because he had so troubled others in his time. - Act. and Mon.
For a warning to others. Aliorum perditio tua sit cautio. It is a just presage and desert of ruin, not to be warned.
paragraphs.anchor: And they raised over him.

paragraphs.text: See Hos 2:15. {See Trapp on "Hos 2:15"}
paragraphs.anchor: The valley of Achor.
